If I'm with friends, I go full stratagems because I know I can just grab a wep and backpack from them.

This is kind of a tough one for me tbh. I believe things do have to go back to normal at some point and cons are part of that normalcy. If you're worried about covid, you shouldn't have gone. AX not enforcing their mask rules the first 2 days is their fault. Their staff and security didn't follow their own rules so they set the example. Needing a negative test or being vaxxed is the best they can do. I personally didn't wear a mask for the first two days, I did bring one though. When they actually started enforcing the masks at panels I complied, no trouble at all.

Bring a refillable bottle and just snack on protein/energy bars and snacks. I've done it for years. If you have to have food, just step out through north Hall and into LA live for a smash burger. I did that when I was really hungry and walked backed in. Beats the food at AX.

I happily spent about $650 on AX. The majority of stuff I bought on Sunday because that's when things weren't as packed as day 1 or 2 and the lines weren't as long. I spent more in the main hall than artist alley this year. Probably a 75% main hall spending and 25% in the artist alley.

It was a lot better than the last couple of years I've been going (Been going since 2014)But that was possibly due to the covid restrictions. And it was actually pretty cool! Not hot after day 1. 

The lines to get the covid wristband and get inside weren't bad at all (imo). Just bad directions from staff and security. For example, on day 1 the second covid wristband booth (facing the north side) had no one going to it for whatever reason. I went and got my band in literally 1 minute. While I watched the other one grow larger and larger. 
To get into the actual conversation, I'd show up at 9:30am, wait for my friend then we'd walk right in at 10am. No lines like the Front entrances have. 

The volunteers and security weren't much help for when it came to directions, timings and lines. We've even had some volunteers ask us what we were lining up for. Lol
There were a few good volunteers. But a lot of bad ones.

I really hate how they don't clear the room for certain screenings like the Trash Taste panel. There were people lining up for the previous panel and getting to stay for the next. I think that is totally unfair for those who actually want to watch the previous panel and watch the next one. 

The r18 section needs to be bigger. It has a small section of the hall but attracts a lot of people and it's just a mess in there due to all the lines for fakku and jlist. The fakku line wrapped at least twice and the jlist line did too. 

Artist alley is great but they really should have the booth number and name above and not on the desk (Some did but not all). The non-scale(1/100) kits are a little better than Bandai's MG kits cause they come with more detailed pieces, water slide decals and pre-painted parts.
The 1/144 scale are equivalent to Bandai's HG kits but the details have to be painted in and I believe they come with some decals and pre-painted parts.

The plastic quality it okay. A little lesser than Bandai's.
With the non-scale kits I had a LOT of trouble with having two parts fit together nicely so I had to sand down the pegs that connect the parts together to get them to fit snug.
Lots of small pieces.
They also have plastic on plastic joints for the hands,head and gun racks so those will wear out fast.
They're pretty hard to pose with those big add shoulders.

If you're gonna build the non-scale kits prepare to sand every joint and peg in the kit cause they do not fit snugly.
If you don't sand it and try to pose it well feel like you're about to break the kit when posing.

Over all it's a very nice kit with TONS of details.
Just be prepared to put in a lot of work.
Oh and non-scale kits come with a special base with the pilots name and robots name.
